About BIMBA Nepal

Health, Longevity & Service

BIMBA Nepal works to improve health, longevity and quality of life through accessible community-based healthcare and support. Our work begins by listening to community needs and connecting people with appropriate health services, specialists, medicines, information and human support.

Mission

To improve health, longevity and quality of life by bringing accessible, community-based healthcare and support closer to people, with particular attention to women, older persons, vulnerable communities and people affected by emergencies.

Vision

Healing Community and Empowering Life. We envision communities where people can access timely health support, age with dignity, and receive care and companionship when life becomes difficult.

Our Values

Human dignity, compassion, inclusion, service, accountability, partnership, prevention, respect for older people and practical community action.

Our Objectives

Promote preventive health, women’s wellbeing, healthy ageing, early identification of health needs, continuity of care, emergency health response and psychosocial wellbeing.

Our Approach

Listen → Identify → Connect → Serve → Respond → Learn. We aim to start with real community needs and strengthen services through experience and partnership.

Our Work

From community health to emergency response

Our first initiatives show an evolving approach: beginning with women’s wellbeing, expanding health and longevity services for older people, and responding when disaster disrupts access to essential care.

Pilot Project of Women Wellbeing

Bhimdhunga Health Camp

Nagarjun Municipality and BIMBA Nepal organized a free health camp at Bhimdhunga Health Post, Nagarjun Municipality–8. The first program placed women and women’s health at the centre while also serving broader community health needs.

Services

  • Video X-ray
  • Radiologist consultation
  • Physician and geriatric consultation
  • Women’s / gynecology consultation
  • Non-communicable disease screening

Reach

137 people registered.

115 received Video X-ray / radiology service.

91 received physician and geriatric consultation.

64 received gynecology consultation.

Community Service

The program brought specialist consultation and screening closer to the community and created a practical starting point for BIMBA Nepal’s women’s wellbeing work.

Pilot Project of Health Longevity Service

Mathatirtha, Chandragiri

Held at Mathatirtha Health Post, Chandragiri Municipality–8, on Shrawan 30, the program focused on people over 60, women and other community members, with healthy and dignified ageing at its centre.

Clinical services

  • Health check-up and medical consultation
  • Blood pressure and blood sugar testing
  • Video X-ray
  • Geriatric consultation
  • Gynecology specialist consultation
  • Pulmonary Function Test and respiratory consultation

Support

Medicines and health materials were provided. Pulmonary services were supported by Cipla Nepal.

Supporting companies included CIPLA-Nepal, Deurali Janta Pharmaceuticals, Magnus Pharma, Intas Pharmaceuticals and Blue Cross Laboratories.

Timely referral

One emergency patient was identified during the program and referred immediately to hospital for further treatment.

The objective was to support long-term health, timely disease identification, proper treatment and health awareness for healthy and respected ageing.

Project under Emergency Response

Bidur–Trishuli Emergency Health Response

Following a flash flood and debris flood affecting communities around Lhende Khola–Bhotekoshi in Rasuwa, BIMBA Nepal, Geriatric Society of Nepal and Art of Living Nepal joined in an emergency health response at the holding center of Ranabhumaneshwar School, Sirkhali, Bidur Municipality–3, Nuwakot.

Why older people needed attention

Many affected older people had lost access to their regular medicines. For people living with chronic conditions, disruption of treatment can become an urgent health concern even when there is no visible injury.

Health services

  • Geriatric examination and consultation
  • Orthopedics and cardiac testing
  • Dental and osteopathy services
  • Trauma relief
  • Stress management
  • Psychosocial counselling
  • Necessary medicines and health materials

Reach

200 people received health examination and medical consultation.

101 were older persons — 48 women and 53 men.

60 older persons and family members received stress-management and psychosocial counselling.

Emergency response is more than treating wounds. People affected by disaster also need human companionship, courage, empathy and hope. Nepal APF Hospital / Armed Police Force, Balambu supported the response with a medical team including doctors deployed locally.

Dignified Ageing

Ageing should not mean losing dignity, voice or access to care.

Dignified Ageing is a signature theme within BIMBA Nepal’s work. It connects health with independence, respect, continuity of care, social connection and the ability to participate meaningfully in community life.

Healthy ageing

Early identification of health needs, preventive care, regular monitoring and appropriate specialist support.

Continuity of care

Helping older people maintain access to essential medicines and services, including during emergencies.

Human connection

Recognizing that wellbeing includes companionship, confidence, empathy and psychosocial support.
